evidence.positive: Against the running build (d638cf09e, demo-demo tenant) staged a colorectal case via the admin API (pathway cefazolin+metronidazole, antibiotic-candidates outcome RECOMMENDED), launched it with POST /api/app-launch, recorded a single 2 g IV cefazolin administration (medication_orders + medication_administrations rows, patient cache evicted from Valkey, confirmed visible via GET /api/admin/patients/{pmrn}/operations/{caseId}/medication-administrations), then fired PROCEDURE_START through POST /api/admin/events/category-event. rule_fired_results for the operation held exactly one antibiotic alert: a-incomplete-antibiotic-pathway with PATHWAY_STATUS=PARTIALLY_GIVEN, medsAdministered [CeFAZolin], missingMeds [MetroNIDAZOLE]. Zero rows for a-known-procedure-missing-antibiotic in rule_fired_results, rule_not_fired_results and rule_failure_results; the engine DEBUG log listed every NOTIFICATION rule evaluated on that event and never named it; GET /api/admin/rule/definitions returned 113 rules without that id and with a-incomplete-antibiotic-pathway present. Repeated on three cases (H, J, plus none-given case A).
evidence.negative: Confirmed the disablement is scoped to the one rule and did not silence the event engine: on the same PROCEDURE_START events the EventBasedRuleEngine evaluated the full NOTIFICATION rule set (log lines for a-eras-antiemetics, a-ebl-antibiotic-redose-reminder, a-antibiotic-infusion-pre-incision-completion, insulin rules etc. with 'Unmatched event categories'), and the replacement rule fired in both the none-given scenario (case A: PATHWAY_STATUS=NONE_GIVEN, ANTIBIOTIC_GROUPS [[CeFAZolin, MetroNIDAZOLE],[CefTRIAXone, MetroNIDAZOLE]]) and the partially-given scenario (cases H and J). The rule_definitions table and the definitions endpoint still carried a-incomplete-antibiotic-pathway, so the pathway guidance remains in place while the retired rule is gone.
evidence.red_check: Pulled StartProcedureMissingAntibioticRule.java as it existed at the OR-2949 merge (commit 65448ac4f, before OR-2944 deleted it), dropped the unused @Slf4j annotation, compiled it inside the app container with javac 25 against the shipped /app/jib-classpath-file (clean compile), backed up the 18-file /app/classes/com/guided/orci/engine/rule/event directory to a tar, copied StartProcedureMissingAntibioticRule.class and StartProcedureMissingAntibioticRule$Group.class into it, and docker-restarted the container (readiness UP after 26 s). Red observed: application log 'Created feature flag for rule: a-known-procedure-missing-antibiotic', a new demo-demo.rule_definitions row for the rule (NOTIFICATION/ALERT/Delayed-Missed-Wrong Antibiotic), GET /api/admin/rule/definitions returned 114 with the id present, and a fresh partially-given colorectal case (case I) fired BOTH a-incomplete-antibiotic-pathway and a-known-procedure-missing-antibiotic on one PROCEDURE_START event (rule_fired_results count 1 for the retired id, log 'Rule evaluated: a-known-procedure-missing-antibiotic -> true'), i.e. the duplicate alert this ticket removes. Reverted: deleted the two class files, md5 of all 18 remaining files matched the backup tar exactly, restarted (readiness UP after 16 s), definitions endpoint back to 113 without the id, and a fresh partially-given case J again fired only a-incomplete-antibiotic-pathway with no retired-rule rows and no retired-rule log lines after the final boot.

caveats: The merged diff (ignore-list entry in EventBasedRuleEngine.getIgnoreRuleList) no longer exists at the built SHA: OR-2944 (#4582, merged after this ticket) deleted StartProcedureMissingAntibioticRule and dropped the entry. Validation covers the delivered outcome (rule unregistered, never evaluated, never fired) rather than the ignore-list mechanism itself.

The cefazolin administration was staged by SQL (medication_orders + medication_administrations with empty JSON lists) plus eviction of the patients/demo-demo/{pmrn} Valkey key, because POST /api/patient/{pmrn}/{caseId}/medication-administration 500s on the demo tenant (MGB HL7 EMR write-back) and the /api/simulation med-admin endpoints hard-code the MGH tenant. The rule read the row through the same ContextPatient path a real administration uses.

RuleService.syncDefinitions upserts but never deletes, so a tenant's rule_definitions keeps a row for a rule removed from code; the engine and /api/admin/rule/definitions ignore it, but anything reading the table directly (analytics joins) would still list a-known-procedure-missing-antibiotic in tenants that ran the old build. Pre-existing OR-2944 side effect, not introduced here.

The red-check boot created a persisted public.feature_flags row RULE:a-known-procedure-missing-antibiotic (enabled) and a demo-demo.rule_definitions row; both survive in this disposable instance only.
Only the demo-demo tenant was exercised; rule registration is tenant-independent (component scan), and the mayo/mgb tenants were not launched.
No UI was exercised; the deliverable has no UI surface beyond the alert itself, which was observed via the rule result tables and admin API.

automation.assessment: Backend: IncompleteAntibioticPathwayRuleTest covers the replacement rule's none-given and partially-given branches; StartProcedureMissingAntibioticRuleTest was deleted with the rule, and there is no test asserting the retired id is absent. qa-suite: clinical-rules/procedure-antibiotics.spec.ts (PABX) covers procedure-start antibiotic guidance but does not assert the alert set is exactly one pathway alert. Worth locking in: the duplicate-alert regression (both rules firing on one PROCEDURE_START) and the catalog exclusion, both cheap and both the substance of this ticket.
proposed_tests: PABX @supplemental: colorectal (cefazolin+metronidazole pathway) case with only cefazolin documented, fire PROCEDURE_START, assert fired rule ids via /api/admin/rule/evaluations/fired contain a-incomplete-antibiotic-pathway with PATHWAY_STATUS PARTIALLY_GIVEN and that no fired, not-fired or failure row names a-known-procedure-missing-antibiotic (red: the same assertion fails if the retired rule is re-registered).

PABX @supplemental: GET /api/admin/rule/definitions excludes a-known-procedure-missing-antibiotic and includes a-incomplete-antibiotic-pathway (guards against the rule being reintroduced or the replacement being dropped).

jira_comment:
Verdict: deploy-ready.

Positive: A colorectal case with only cefazolin documented was started on the shipped build and only a-incomplete-antibiotic-pathway fired, with no evaluation, firing, or catalog entry for a-known-procedure-missing-antibiotic.
Negative: The same procedure-start event still ran the full event rule set, and the replacement rule fired in both the none-given and partially-given scenarios, so only the retired rule is gone.
Red check: Compiling the pre-removal rule class back into the running container made the retired rule register and fire a second alert on the same event, and removing it restored the single alert.

Automation: A supplemental PABX test asserting exactly one antibiotic-pathway alert at procedure start plus a definitions-endpoint exclusion check are proposed.
